metadata.disclaimer: OSA's own analysis of BSI's Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5:2026 against SP 800-53 Rev 5. C5:2026 is by Germany's Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), published in April 2026 and licensed CC BY-ND 4.0. OSA uses BSI's criterion and sub-criterion ids. The titles, pairs, rationale and gaps are OSA's own. Each clause is one of C5's 168 criteria, read with its optional additional criteria, which are folded into it. The coverage figure estimates how much of the criterion and its additional criteria the listed controls meet when put in place as written. C5 is written for cloud service providers, so read each control as applying to the provider and the systems that run its cloud service. Read BSI's text at bsi.bund.de, and check each criterion against it before you use this mapping for compliance or audit work.
metadata.applicability_note: Cloud customers ask providers for a C5 attestation, an auditor's report on how the provider meets the criteria. German law asks for C5 in two places. Federal bodies set C5's basic criteria as the minimum security requirements for the external cloud services they use, under BSI's minimum standard for external cloud services. Healthcare providers, statutory health and care insurers and the firms that process data for them may put social and health data in a cloud service only where it holds a current C5 attestation on the basic criteria, of Type 2 since 1 July 2025, or a certificate of comparable or higher level (section 393 of Book V of the Social Code, SGB V).

clause_fields.basic_criteria: the ids of BSI's basic criteria for the criterion, such as OIS-01.01B
clause_fields.additional_criteria: the ids of BSI's optional additional criteria, folded into the criterion. An id ending AS sharpens a basic criterion, and one ending AC adds to it

edition.used: C5:2026, English version 1.0.2, with one change from BSI's German version 1.1.1: the English AM-01.02AC, on keeping the asset inventory up to date, is AM-02.01AC, as in the German version.
edition.in_force: BSI published C5:2026 as final at the end of March 2026. BSI recommends it for audit periods ending on or after 1 June 2027, and C5:2020 for audit periods ending before then.
edition.german_version: BSI's German version 1.1.1 brings corrections of August 2026 that the English version 1.0.2 does not yet have. OSA compared the two, sub-criterion by sub-criterion, and found 31 differences in what a sub-criterion asks, most of them small. The German is narrower in some, such as CRY-04.01AS, whose duty to encrypt covers public networks only, and asks for more in others, such as HR-05.01B, which asks for proof that staff were told of their lasting duties. None changes which controls the mapping lists. OSA rated the English text and checks the mapping again when BSI publishes the English corrections.

analysis.basis: OSA's own analysis, from BSI's text by three independent ratings. NIST's catalogue of registered crosswalks has none for C5 (checked 12 November 2026), and BSI publishes no mapping to SP 800-53. BSI licenses C5:2026 under CC BY-ND 4.0, which allows it to be shared only unchanged, and OSA's data is CC BY-SA 4.0, so OSA rated the criteria itself and wrote the titles, rationale and gaps in its own words.

analysis.controls: SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 base controls. An enhancement that meets a criterion counts for its base control. Controls that Rev 5 withdrew are not used.
analysis.method: Six AI raters worked in two groups of three. One group rated the 76 criteria of the domains OIS to OPS, and the other the 92 of IAM to PSS. Each rater worked on its own, from BSI's English text of each criterion and BSI's supplementary information, and from the control statements. None saw another's rating. Each rater read a criterion together with its additional criteria and rated them as one. OSA lists a control for a criterion where at least two of the three raters in its group named it, or where OSA's house rule for policy clauses adds it. The coverage figure is the median of the three estimates of how much of the criterion and its additional criteria an organisation would meet by putting the listed controls in place. OSA wrote the titles, rationale and gaps after the controls were settled, from the raters' reasons and the gaps at least two of them named, and a reviewer checked each one against the control statements.
analysis.agreement_measure: The Jaccard index of each two ratings: the pairs both named, divided by the pairs either named.

agreement_by_group.criteria_rated: Domains OIS, SP, HR, AM, PS and OPS
Domains IAM, CRY, COS, PI, DEV, SSO, SIM, BCM, COM, INQ and PSS

analysis.agreement_by_group_note: Each group had its own three ratings, A, B and C. The overall figures pool the ratings with the same letter across the two groups. By group, the index runs from 0.74 to 0.84.
analysis.coverage_agreement: The three coverage estimates for a criterion lie within 10 points of each other for 147 of the 168 criteria. The widest spread is 25 points, for SSO-06, PS-01, INQ-03, INQ-01 and CRY-12.
analysis.pairs_note: The file lists 699 pairs over 183 controls: the 590 named by all three ratings and the 109 named by two. OIS-02, SP-01 and SP-02 list PM-01 with every other family's -01 control, as OSA's rule for policy clauses asks, and at least two raters named each of those pairs. 87 of the 168 criteria list one to three controls. Apart from the policy clauses, OPS-34 lists the most, 15, followed by AM-12 with 13. OPS-03, PI-02, INQ-02 and INQ-04 list no control, because no control was named by two raters.

policy_rule.rule: OSA's house rule for policy clauses, set on 1 November 2026: a clause that asks for security policies in general lists PM-01 with every other family's -01 control, the set NIST's crosswalk gives ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.5.1, and PT-01 as well where it covers personal data.
policy_rule.note: OIS-02 asks for the overall information security policy, SP-01 for the policies and procedures derived from it, and SP-02 for their review at least once a year. The raters' brief gave them the rule, and at least two of them named all 19 controls for each of the three, so the rule adds no pairs of its own. None of them covers personal data, so PT-01 stays out.

analysis.not_mapped: Every criterion is mapped: the 462 basic criteria and 161 additional criteria are folded into their 168 criteria, and each clause lists their ids. C5 also asks a provider to describe six general conditions in its system description, GC-01 to GC-06, such as the law that applies, availability and recovery figures and its certifications. They are disclosures rather than security criteria, so OSA leaves them out. So are the complementary customer criteria, which BSI writes for the cloud customer.

clauses.title: An ISO 27001 management system that covers the cloud service
clauses.rationale: PM-01 has the provider write an organisation-wide security programme plan that sets out its requirements and assigns roles and responsibilities. A senior official approves the plan, and the provider reviews and updates it on a set cycle, which gives the documented core of a management system. PL-02 has the security plan define the system's components and its links to other systems, and describe the controls in place with the reasons for any tailoring. That records the scope and boundaries of the service and serves as a statement of applicability. CA-02 has the controls assessed on a set cycle, and CA-02(01) uses independent assessors, which comes part of the way to a certification audit.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for an ISMS that meets ISO/IEC 27001, with the provider's context and the results of the last management review on record. Add both to the programme plan. The additional criteria ask for a valid certificate from an accredited certification body.

clauses.title: A top-level security policy set by senior management
clauses.rationale: This criterion lists PM-01 with the -01 control of every other family except PT, as OSA does for clauses that ask for security policies in general. PM-01 gives an organisation-wide security programme plan with assigned roles and management commitment, approved by a senior official who is accountable for the risk. Each -01 control adds a documented policy for its own family that covers purpose, scope, roles and management commitment, shared with defined roles and reviewed on a set cycle. Together they give a top-level policy approved by senior management, with a policy for each area beneath it.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks top management to share the policy with customers as well as with the provider's own and external staff. Extend the distribution under PM-01 to customers. C5 also asks the policy to state security objectives with a target level of security, and the strategy for reaching them.

clauses.title: Shared responsibility model with customers
clauses.rationale: CA-03 has the provider manage each information exchange through agreements, such as service level or user agreements. Each agreement records the interface, the security requirements, the controls and the responsibilities of each side, and the provider reviews it on a set cycle. PL-02 has the security plan describe dependencies on and connections to other systems, and the provider tells defined roles about later changes to the plan. SA-05 gives customers user documentation on the security functions open to them and on their own part in keeping the service secure. SA-09 defines and documents oversight and user roles for the external services the provider relies on.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for one documented model that splits the handling of vulnerabilities and incidents between the provider and its customers. Set out that split in the CA-03 agreements and the SA-05 user documentation. Announce changes to the model early enough for customers to adapt before they take effect.

clauses.title: Separating conflicting duties on the basis of risk
clauses.rationale: AC-05 has the provider identify and document the duties that need separating and define access rights that support the separation, which gives the list of conflicts. AC-02 sets prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership and reviews accounts on a set cycle, so the separation holds whenever roles are assigned or changed. CM-05 defines and enforces access restrictions for changes to the system, and CM-05(05) limits privileges in production and operation, which helps keep development apart from operations. Where duties stay combined, AU-06 reviews audit records for inappropriate or unusual activity and reports the findings.
clauses.gaps: C5 bases the separation on a risk assessment that covers role administration, the release of changes, risk management and operations. Run that assessment and record the resulting measures in the risk treatment plan. The additional criteria ask the provider to monitor the separation measures and fix deviations promptly.

clauses.title: Gathering threat intelligence and feeding it into risk management
clauses.rationale: PM-16 sets up a threat awareness programme that shares threat intelligence across organisations. SI-05 has the provider receive security alerts and advisories from outside bodies on an ongoing basis and issue internal ones where needed. RA-03 identifies threats to the system as part of the risk assessment. RA-03(02) uses all-source intelligence and RA-03(03) adds dynamic threat awareness, which bring the intelligence into risk management.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to correlate the threat information with its own assets and processes to judge the likely impact. Add that step to the RA-03 assessment, and include internal sources such as the provider's own security monitoring.

clauses.title: Keeping in touch with Germany's national cyber bodies
clauses.rationale: PM-15 has the provider set up and keep contact with chosen groups in the security community to share current information on threats and incidents. SI-05 has it receive security alerts and advisories from defined outside bodies on an ongoing basis. IR-06 has it report incident information to the authorities it names. With the national centre and the CERT association named as those bodies, these controls give the contact C5 asks for.
clauses.gaps: C5 names the BSI's CERT association and the National IT Situation Centre, and applies when German public sector bodies use the service. Name both as the outside bodies in these controls whenever the service has such customers.

clauses.title: A documented, repeatable method for managing risk
clauses.rationale: RA-01 gives a documented risk assessment policy with procedures to carry it out, shared with defined roles and reviewed on a set cycle. PM-09 sets one strategy for managing security risk and applies it consistently across the organisation, which gives a common basis for comparing results. PM-28 records the assumptions, constraints, priorities and risk tolerance that serve as criteria for accepting and ranking risks. RA-03 identifies threats and vulnerabilities and judges the likelihood and size of harm, with the results documented. RA-07 responds to findings in line with the risk tolerance, which covers the treatment step.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a method that gives comparable and reproducible results, with a named owner for each risk who approves its treatment and accepts the residual risk. Assign those owners in the RA-01 procedures. Have the management level responsible for the service's security review the assessment and the status of treatment plans.

clauses.title: Yearly and event-driven risk assessment of the service
clauses.rationale: RA-01 provides the documented risk assessment policy and procedures that C5 asks the provider to put in place. RA-03 has the provider document risk assessments and share the results with defined roles. It updates them on a set cycle or after significant changes, and RA-03(01) adds supply chain risk, which covers dependence on service organisations. CA-07 continuous monitoring, with CA-07(04) risk monitoring, follows how risks develop. PM-09 applies one security risk strategy across the organisation, and PM-29 appoints a senior official who aligns risk management with strategic planning, which meets the additional criterion on enterprise risk.
clauses.gaps: C5 lists risk sources to weigh, such as tenant separation, interfaces open to public networks, key management and insider threats. Add them to the RA-03 assessment and run it at least once a year. Have risk owners review the analysis and treatment each year, and give customers and other outside parties the results that concern them.

clauses.title: Planning and tracking the treatment of risks
clauses.rationale: CA-05 has the provider keep a plan of action and milestones for remedying weaknesses and known vulnerabilities, updated from assessments and monitoring. PM-04 makes sure those plans record the remedial actions and are reported as required, and checks them against the risk strategy and organisation-wide priorities. RA-07 has the provider respond to findings in line with its risk tolerance, which brings risk down to a level that can be accepted. SA-05 user documentation sets out the users' part in keeping the service secure, which is where shared risks meet the customer's own controls.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks risk owners to accept the residual risk and to review the chosen treatment options whenever the risk assessment changes. Add both steps to the CA-05 process. Decide, from contracts and the law, which outside parties receive information on the treatment plan and how much.

clauses.title: Assessing security risk in projects that affect the service
clauses.rationale: SA-03 has the provider manage the system through a development life cycle that builds in security, with security roles defined. It also brings the organisation's risk management process into the life cycle activities. RA-03 has the provider update the risk assessment when the system or its environment changes significantly, which covers the risks a project brings.
clauses.gaps: C5 covers every project that may affect the service, including organisational changes outside system development. Bring those projects under the RA-03 assessment and treat the risks it finds.

clauses.title: One consistent, approved set of security policies
clauses.rationale: This criterion lists PM-01 with the -01 control of every other family except PT, as OSA does for clauses that ask for security policies in general. PM-01 gives the organisation-wide programme plan, approved by a senior official, from which the other policies follow. Each -01 control has the provider document a policy for its family that covers purpose, scope, roles and responsibilities, with procedures to carry it out. The provider shares each one with defined roles and names an official to manage it.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks every policy to derive from the top-level policy and follow one structure, with version control and approval by top management or an authorised body. Add these rules to the -01 controls. In each policy, also name the qualifications and stand-ins for its roles, and its dependencies on customers and subservice organisations.

clauses.title: Yearly expert review of security policies, approved before use
clauses.rationale: This criterion lists PM-01 with the -01 control of every other family except PT, as OSA does for clauses that ask for security policies in general. Each -01 control has the provider review and update its family's policy and procedures on a set cycle and after defined events. PM-01 has a senior official approve the programme plan, which the provider also reviews and updates on a set cycle and after defined events. Together they keep the whole policy set under regular and event-driven review.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks subject matter experts to review each policy at least once a year and after significant changes to the service, weighing organisational and technical changes along with new legal duties. Set that cycle and those inputs in each -01 control. Have the right level of management approve revised policies before they take effect.

clauses.title: A risk-approved register of policy exceptions
clauses.rationale: CM-06 has the provider record and approve any departure from its set configuration settings, which handles technical exceptions. CA-05 keeps a plan of action and milestones for known weaknesses and updates it on a set cycle, which tracks open exceptions and their remediation. RA-07 has the provider respond to findings in line with its risk tolerance, which gives the risk decision each exception needs.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for one register of every exception to a security policy, with its controls and a set period of validity. Keep that register and review it at least once a year, weighing the combined risk of all the exceptions. Allow only exceptions that leave every applicable C5 criterion met, and watch the register so approvals stay current, as the additional criteria ask.

clauses.title: Screening staff who can reach production systems and data
clauses.rationale: PS-02 gives every position a risk designation with screening criteria for the people who fill it, and reviews the designations on a set cycle, which classifies sensitive roles by risk. PS-03 screens people before they get access and rescreens them under conditions and at a frequency the provider sets, which covers checks before hiring and before a move into a riskier role. PS-05 reviews and adjusts access when people are reassigned or transferred. PS-07 sets personnel security requirements for external providers and has them follow the provider's policies, which extends the checks to external staff. PS-01 gives the personnel security policy, where the positions that need regular checks are defined.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to name the roles that can reach customer data or production components. C5 has the provider check competence as well as integrity for those roles, with measures such as identity papers, CVs, degrees, a police certificate and exposure to blackmail where local law allows. Record the roles and set those checks as screening criteria in PS-02, then run them under PS-03.

clauses.title: Security duties written into staff contracts
clauses.rationale: PL-04 gives each person who needs access rules that set out their duties and expected behaviour, and takes a documented acknowledgement before access is granted. PS-06 has people sign access agreements, such as non-disclosure and acceptable use agreements, before they get access, and sign again after updates. PS-07 has external providers follow the provider's personnel security policies and procedures, which binds external staff to the same rules.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for employment terms that reflect the law and bind staff to a code of ethics as well as the security policy. Add both to the contracts and to the PL-04 rules. Make the non-disclosure clause in PS-06 cover all information staff gain or create in the service, including anonymised information.

clauses.title: Role-based security awareness and training for all staff
clauses.rationale: AT-02 gives all users, contractors included, security literacy training when they start and on a set cycle, updated with lessons from incidents. AT-02(06) covers the current cyber threat environment. AT-03 adds role-based training before access and when systems change, and IR-02 gives users incident response training that fits their roles. AT-04 documents and monitors training and keeps individual records, which tracks completion, and AT-06 reports training results to defined staff, which supports evaluating the programme.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to measure learning outcomes for each target group, with quantitative and qualitative measures. Add those measures to the AT-06 feedback. Follow up promptly on any missed training that the AT-04 records show.

clauses.title: A documented disciplinary process for policy breaches
clauses.rationale: PS-08 runs a formal sanctions process for people who break security policies and procedures. When a sanction starts, it tells defined roles who is sanctioned and why, which leaves a record of each use. PS-01 gives a personnel security policy and procedures consistent with applicable law, where the disciplinary process is set down.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the process to confirm that a breach took place and to weigh its severity and impact before acting. Add both steps to the PS-08 process. Tell all internal and external staff in advance what measures they may face.

clauses.title: Security duties that continue after leaving or changing jobs
clauses.rationale: PS-04 holds exit interviews that cover the security topics the provider sets, and PS-04(01) adds the post-employment requirements that departing staff are told about. PS-06(03) does the same through the access agreements under PS-06, which make people aware of duties that continue after they leave.
clauses.gaps: C5 covers staff who change roles as well as those who leave. Tell both groups which duties stay in place, and state in the access agreements how long each one lasts.

clauses.title: Confidentiality agreements for staff and service organisations
clauses.rationale: PS-06 has the provider write access agreements, such as non-disclosure agreements, and review and update them on a set cycle. People sign them before they get access and sign again when the agreements change, which gives the renewed confirmation C5 asks for. PS-07 sets personnel security requirements for external providers and has them follow the provider's policies, which brings service organisations under the confidentiality terms.
clauses.gaps: C5 bases the agreements on the provider's documented needs for protecting confidential information, with a review of those needs every year and after significant changes. Have service organisations accept the agreement when they sign the contract. Where staff or a service organisation decline an update, assess the resulting risk.

clauses.title: Rules for protecting information when staff work remotely
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and PE-01 give documented and shared policies with procedures for access control and physical protection, which hold the rules for staff working off site. AC-17 documents the restrictions and connection requirements for each type of remote access, and AC-17(02) protects remote sessions with encryption. AC-19 sets configuration and connection requirements for the provider's mobile devices, also outside controlled areas, which covers approved equipment. AC-20 sets terms for external systems or bans them, and AC-20(03) restricts the use of systems owned by others, which covers personal devices. PE-17 documents the alternate work sites staff may use and the controls that apply there, with a way to reach security staff about incidents.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for guidance to staff on handling and storing sensitive information at home and in public places. Add it to the controls set for alternate work sites in PE-17.

clauses.title: Putting the remote working rules into practice
clauses.rationale: AC-17 authorises each type of remote access before connections are allowed, with AC-17(01) monitoring and controlling it and AC-17(02) encrypting it. AC-19 applies configuration requirements to the provider's mobile devices and authorises their connection, and AC-19(05) adds full device or container encryption. AC-20 enforces the terms for external systems or bans them, which keeps unmanaged devices out. PE-17 applies defined controls at alternate work sites and assesses how well they work.
clauses.gaps: C5 expects protection on the endpoints staff use away from the office. Add it to the PE-17 controls, and check that the measures let staff follow the remote working policy in practice.

clauses.title: Documented rules for identifying and tracking service assets
clauses.rationale: CM-01 gives a documented and shared configuration management policy with procedures, which hold the asset framework. CM-08 has the provider document an inventory of system components at the level of detail needed for tracking and reporting, which sets how assets are inventoried. CM-09 sets a configuration management plan with a process for identifying configuration items through the development life cycle and placing them under management. RA-02 categorises the system and the information it handles, with the reasons on record, which gives the scheme for protection needs.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the framework to define asset types, keeping hardware apart from software, with a life cycle for each type. Add both to the CM-09 plan. The additional criterion asks the provider to use asset data in logging and monitoring to judge the impact of events and to inform affected customers.

clauses.title: Keeping a complete, current inventory of assets
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an accurate inventory that holds every component once, with the information needed for accountability, and the provider reviews and updates it on a set cycle. CM-08(01) and CM-08(02) keep it current as components come and go, using automation, and CM-08(03) detects unauthorised components. CM-12 documents the users who can reach the components where defined information is processed and stored. AC-02 records each account's authorised users with their group and role membership and their access rights.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to log every change to an asset's record. C5 also asks each asset's record to hold the information the risk procedure needs and the measures taken against those risks. Add both to the CM-08 inventory.

clauses.title: Details recorded for each hardware item
clauses.rationale: CM-08 has each inventory entry hold the information the provider needs for component accountability, at a level of detail fit for tracking. CM-08(04) adds accountability information, such as who is responsible for each component, and CM-08(08) tracks location automatically.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks each hardware entry to show where the asset stands in its life cycle and to carry the information needed for its risk assessment. Add both fields to the CM-08 inventory.

clauses.title: A full record of the software the service uses
clauses.rationale: CM-08 inventories every system component, software included, at a level of detail fit for tracking and with the information needed for accountability. The provider reviews and updates the inventory on a set cycle, which identifies each software asset and keeps the record current.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks each software entry to show which other assets use it. The additional criterion adds how long the supplier will provide security updates, where the supplier has said so. Record both in the CM-08 inventory.

clauses.title: Rules for using assets securely through their life cycle
clauses.rationale: CM-01, MA-01, MP-01, PE-01, SA-01 and SI-01 give documented and shared policies with procedures for configuration, maintenance, media, physical protection, acquisition and system integrity, which hold the asset rules across the life cycle. CM-06 sets restrictive configuration settings for components and approves any departures, which covers the secure set-up of security mechanisms. CM-11 governs software that users install, and MP-07 restricts or bans defined media types and bans ownerless portable storage. SA-22 replaces components once their supplier stops support, or arranges other support, which deals with software whose security patches have ended.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to set approval steps for each stage of an asset's life, from acquisition to disposal, and rules for disabling or wiping assets remotely. Add both to the asset rules under CM-01 and MP-01.

clauses.title: Approving new hardware before it enters production
clauses.rationale: CM-03 reviews proposed changes and approves or rejects them with explicit regard to security impact analyses, and records the decisions, which gives an approval step for bringing hardware into production. CM-04 analyses each change for its security impact before it is made, and CM-04(02) checks afterwards that the affected controls work as intended. CM-06 sets and applies secure configuration settings for components, which is what the provider checks before approval.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for approval only after a check of the hardware's error handling, logging, encryption and access mechanisms against its intended use. List those checks in the CM-03 approval step, and treat the risks found before approval is given.

clauses.title: Retiring hardware with secure deletion or destruction
clauses.rationale: MP-01 gives documented media protection procedures, which hold the steps for retiring hardware that stores data. MP-06 sanitises media before they are disposed of or reused, with mechanisms as strong as the information's classification requires. MP-06(01) adds review, approval, tracking and verification of that sanitisation. SR-12 disposes of defined data and components with defined techniques, which covers destroying the media.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a decommissioning procedure in its own right, with approval by authorised staff before the hardware is retired. Write it into the MP-01 procedures.

clauses.title: Staff commitments on handling and returning assets
clauses.rationale: PL-04 gives people rules for using information and systems and takes a documented acknowledgement before access, which proves their commitment. PS-06 has them sign access agreements, such as acceptable use agreements, before they get access. On termination, PS-04 retrieves all security-related property, disables system access within a set time and revokes credentials, which covers the return of assets and the removal of access.
clauses.gaps: C5 uses a risk assessment to decide which assets need a provable commitment, namely those where loss or unauthorised access could harm the service. Run that assessment, and keep proof that each asset handed out came back.

clauses.title: Classifying assets by the protection needs of their data
clauses.rationale: RA-02 categorises the system and the information it handles, with the reasons recorded and the decision approved, which classifies assets by the protection needs of their data. RA-02(01) adds a finer ranking within each impact level. MP-03 marks media with distribution limits and handling caveats, and PE-22 marks hardware components with the impact or classification level of the information they may handle. IA-03 identifies and authenticates defined devices uniquely before a connection is made, which meets the additional criterion on device identity.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a review of classification levels at least once a year and after significant changes, with a schema that also covers authenticity and matches the recovery objectives. Add both to the RA-02 categorisation. The additional criteria ask monitoring to rank events by the protection need of the asset involved.

clauses.title: Storing idle hardware safely until it is needed
clauses.rationale: MP-04 keeps defined media under physical control and stores them securely in controlled areas until they are destroyed or sanitised, which protects idle hardware that holds data. PE-18 places system components to limit damage from hazards and the chance of unauthorised access. MP-01 and PE-01 give documented media and physical protection procedures, which can hold the procedure for hardware on hold.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a documented procedure, based on a risk assessment, for hardware that is temporarily out of use. Write it into the MP-01 and PE-01 procedures.

clauses.title: Moving production hardware off site under control
clauses.rationale: PE-16 authorises and controls components entering and leaving the facility and keeps records of them. MA-02 has defined roles approve explicitly any removal of components for off-site repair or replacement. MP-05 protects media in transport outside controlled areas, keeps accountability, documents the transport and limits it to authorised staff, and MP-05(03) adds custodians for the chain of custody. MP-01 and PE-01 give the documented procedures for these moves.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for checks on receipt and protection against tampering in transit, with the transfer method chosen on the basis of a risk assessment. Add these to the MP-05 transport controls.

clauses.title: Securing portable storage and the devices staff use
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and MP-01 give the documented policies that hold the rules for endpoints and removable media, and MP-07 restricts or bans defined media types and bans ownerless portable storage. SC-28(01) encrypts stored information on endpoints and media under SC-28, AC-19(05) encrypts the provider's mobile devices under AC-19, and SI-03 scans files from external sources at endpoints as they are opened or run. CM-07 restricts defined functions, such as running programs automatically from removable storage, and AC-11 locks an idle device until the user signs in again. MP-05 protects media in transport outside controlled areas, including equipment on its way to disposal, and MP-06 sanitises media before they leave the provider's control or are reused. PL-04 sets users' duties for using systems securely, which covers devices and media. AC-20 sets terms for third-party systems, and SC-07(12) and SC-07(10) add host-based protection and exfiltration prevention under SC-07 for the additional criteria.
clauses.gaps: C5 bases the endpoint and media measures on a risk assessment. Run it and record the results in the AC-01 and MP-01 procedures. The additional criteria also ask for remote location tracking on managed mobile devices.

clauses.title: Site security requirements for data centres and premises
clauses.rationale: PE-01 gives a documented and shared physical and environmental protection policy with procedures, which records the security requirements for premises. PE-23 plans the facility's location with physical and environmental hazards in mind and weighs those hazards for existing sites, which addresses faults in planning. PE-11 provides an uninterruptible power supply for an orderly shutdown or a move to long-term alternate power, and PE-11(01) and PE-11(02) add an alternate power supply. SA-09 has the operators of external services meet the provider's security requirements and use defined controls, and monitors their compliance, which covers data centres run by service organisations.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to define at least a sensitive and a public security area, and to set data centre requirements against each hazard it lists. Write both into the PE-01 policy, with the longest utility outage each facility can tolerate under the service level agreement. The additional criteria set design figures for self-sufficient running, such as 72 hours on the site's own power supply.

clauses.title: Running the service from at least two separate sites
clauses.rationale: SC-36 spreads defined processing and storage components across several physical locations, which supports running the service from more than one site. CP-07 sets up an alternate processing site with controls equal to those at the primary site, able to resume operations within the recovery objectives. CP-07(01) keeps that site far enough from the primary to reduce exposure to the same threats. CP-04 tests the contingency plan on a set cycle, and CP-04(02) tests the alternate site, which checks that the redundancy works.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the service to run from at least two sites that meet the provider's security requirements, with redundancy designed to meet the availability in the service level agreement. Size the CP-07 and SC-36 arrangements to that figure. The additional criteria ask for a third site that keeps the service running if two fail together.

clauses.title: A solid building shell that resists and detects intrusion
clauses.rationale: PE-03 enforces access authorisations at entry and exit points with access control systems or guards. PE-03(03) adds continuous guards and PE-03(07) adds physical barriers. PE-06 monitors physical access to detect and respond to incidents, and PE-06(01) and PE-06(03) add intrusion alarms and video surveillance. AT-03 role-based training, with AT-03(02) on physical security controls, prepares data centre staff to respond to intrusion attempts.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a solid building shell whose outer elements together hold off a break-in for at least ten minutes, with walls and locks to match. Specify that resistance for each site, and add compensating measures where the elements fall short.

clauses.title: Controlling and logging entry to sites and secure areas
clauses.rationale: PE-02 keeps an approved list of people allowed into the facility, issues credentials, reviews the list and removes people once their need for access ends. PE-02(01) grants access by position or role, which supports least privilege. PE-03 checks each person's authorisation before entry, controls entry and exit with access control systems, keeps access logs and escorts visitors. PE-06 monitors physical access and reviews the logs, which lets the provider check that only authorised people entered, and PE-08 keeps and reviews visitor records and reports anomalies. PE-01 gives the documented policy and procedures for these rules.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to revoke physical access left unused for two months and to require multi-factor authentication for areas hosting customer data systems. Add both to the PE-02 and PE-03 rules. C5 also asks for warning signs at non-public areas and a review after every emergency override of access control.

clauses.title: Protecting the sites from environmental hazards
clauses.rationale: PE-13 keeps fire detection and suppression systems running on an independent energy source. PE-13(01) and PE-13(02) activate them automatically and send notifications, and PE-13(04) adds inspections. PE-10 lets staff shut off power to components in an emergency, which supports cutting power when fire is detected. PE-09 protects power equipment and cabling from damage, and PE-09(02) adds automatic voltage controls against overvoltage. PE-15 protects the system from water leaks with working shutoff valves, and PE-23 plans the site with physical and environmental hazards in mind, which covers flood levels.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for fire sections whose structural parts resist fire for at least 90 minutes, or equivalent measures, and for protection against lightning and heavy rain. Specify these for each site. C5 also asks for regular fire drills: schedule them alongside the PE-13 inspections.

clauses.title: Keeping power and other supply facilities running
clauses.rationale: PE-11 provides an uninterruptible power supply for an orderly shutdown or a move to long-term alternate power, and PE-11(01) and PE-11(02) add an alternate power supply. PE-09 protects power equipment and cabling from damage, with PE-09(01) adding redundant cabling, and PE-04 controls physical access to distribution and transmission lines. CP-08 sets up alternate telecommunications services, with CP-08(02) addressing single points of failure and CP-08(03) separating the primary and alternate providers. PE-14 keeps temperature and humidity within set levels, which the cooling supply must achieve, and MA-02 schedules and documents maintenance in line with manufacturer specifications.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for N+1 redundancy in power and cooling, with the backup power tested at least once a year. Have qualified staff inspect distributors and cabling at least every two years for tampering and for agreement with the documentation. The additional criteria size the cooling for five days of the hottest expected weather.

clauses.title: Monitoring utilities and room conditions with alarms
clauses.rationale: PE-14 keeps environmental levels such as temperature and humidity within set limits and monitors them on a set cycle. PE-14(01) adds automatic controls and PE-14(02) raises alarms and notifications when levels go out of range. PE-15(01) detects water near the system and alerts staff by automated means, which covers leak alarms under PE-15.
clauses.gaps: C5 also asks the provider to monitor the operating parameters of the utilities, such as the power supply and the uninterruptible power systems. Bring them into the same monitoring and alarms as PE-14.

clauses.title: Security rules for office workplaces
clauses.rationale: PE-01 gives the documented physical protection policy that holds the office requirements. PE-03 enforces access authorisations at entry points with access control systems or guards, and PE-06 monitors physical access, with PE-06(01) and PE-06(03) adding intrusion alarms and video surveillance. AC-11 locks idle devices and AC-11(01) hides the screen content, while MP-04 keeps media, paper included, under control and stored securely. MP-06 sanitises media before disposal, which covers destroying unneeded documents, and AC-20 lets the provider ban defined types of external systems, such as third-party equipment.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for privacy screens on workstations. C5 also bases the office requirements on a risk assessment and lets the provider scale them for rented offices. Record that assessment and the resulting requirements in the PE-01 policy.

clauses.title: Planning staff and system capacity ahead of demand
clauses.rationale: CP-02(02) adds capacity planning to the contingency plan under CP-02, so that the needed capacity exists during contingency operations. SC-06 allocates defined resources by priority or quota, which helps keep agreed resources available to customers when capacity runs short.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a standing procedure that plans staff and system capacity for normal operations and forecasts demand from usage trends. Set one up, and use the forecasts with the service level agreement when planning provisioning.

clauses.title: Watching capacity so customers get what was agreed
clauses.rationale: SC-05(03) adds detection and monitoring to the denial-of-service protection of SC-05, which has the provider watch defined system resources to see whether enough exist. SC-06 allocates defined resources by priority or quota, which helps deliver resources as agreed with each customer.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for procedures to provision and release resources and to check that the service level agreements are met. Set them up, and report to customers any capacity shortfall that breaches the contract. The additional criterion offers customers a self-service view of capacity and availability.

clauses.title: Customer control over allocated resources
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 sets controls for an organisation's own systems, while this criterion concerns a feature the provider offers its customers: the means to steer and monitor the resources allocated to them. C5 also asks the provider to tell customers about significant security changes to those resources. Build both into the service and its customer documentation.

clauses.title: Rules for protecting systems and devices from malware
clauses.rationale: SI-01 gives a documented and shared system and information integrity policy with procedures, which holds the malware rules. SI-03 places malicious code protection at system entry and exit points and updates it automatically. It runs periodic scans of the system and real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoints and network entry points, which covers staff devices as well as incoming traffic.
clauses.gaps: C5 also asks the policy to cover the protection mechanisms built into each system. Name them in the SI-01 procedures.

clauses.title: Running and updating malware protection in production
clauses.rationale: SI-03 puts malicious code protection on the system and updates it automatically as new releases appear. It alerts defined staff when it finds malicious code. CM-06 monitors and controls changes to configuration settings, and CM-06(01) and CM-06(02) verify the settings automatically and respond to unauthorised changes, which covers the additional criteria on monitoring the protection set-up. AU-06 reviews and analyses records, such as scan results, on a set cycle and reports the findings to defined roles.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for malware definitions to be updated at least daily, or as often as the vendor allows under the additional criteria. Set that frequency in SI-03. The additional criteria also ask the provider to secure the customer and administration consoles against malware.

clauses.title: Backup and restore rules matched to recovery objectives
clauses.rationale: CP-01 gives a documented and shared contingency planning policy with procedures, which holds the backup and restore rules. CP-09 backs up information at a frequency that fits the recovery time and recovery point objectives and protects the backup information. CP-09(08) encrypts the backups. CP-10 recovers and rebuilds the system to a known state within a time that fits the recovery objectives, which covers restores.
clauses.gaps: C5 sets the scope and retention of backups by the customer contracts as well as by the recovery objectives. Align the CP-09 schedule with those contracts. Where the contract provides for it, handle restores and restore tests that customers request.

clauses.title: Watching backup runs and fixing failures
clauses.rationale: CP-09 runs backups at the frequency the recovery objectives set, and CP-09(01) tests the backups for reliability and integrity, which partly confirms that they ran as planned. IR-04 gives an incident handling capability that covers detection, analysis, containment and recovery, which covers investigating and fixing failed backups.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to monitor every backup run against the backup policy, and to investigate and fix failures in time to meet customer obligations. Set up that monitoring alongside CP-09. The additional criterion gives customers backup logs or summaries in a self-service portal.

clauses.title: Testing restores against recovery objectives each year
clauses.rationale: CP-04 tests the contingency plan on a set cycle and starts corrective action where the results call for it. CP-04(04) tests full recovery and reconstitution, and CP-04(01) coordinates the tests with related plans. CP-09(01) tests backups for reliability and integrity, and CP-09(02) restores samples during testing under CP-09. SA-03(02) controls the use of live data in preproduction environments under SA-03, which supports restoring customer data only where production access rules apply.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for restore tests at least once a year, judged against the contract terms and the recovery time and point objectives. Record each test in full, including how the restored data was then securely deleted. The additional criteria ask the provider to share the results with customers who request them.

clauses.title: Keeping protected backups at a distant second site
clauses.rationale: CP-06 sets up an alternate storage site with controls equal to those at the primary site, and CP-06(01) keeps it far enough from the primary site to reduce shared threats. CP-09 protects backup information, with CP-09(05) transferring backups to the alternate site and CP-09(08) encrypting them. MP-05 protects backup media carried outside controlled areas, and SC-08(01) encrypts backups sent over a network under SC-08.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to choose the distance between sites by weighing recovery times against the impact a disaster could have on both. Record that reasoning when siting the CP-06 storage site.

clauses.title: A policy for event logging and system monitoring
clauses.rationale: AU-01 and SI-01 give documented and shared policies with procedures for logging and for system integrity, which set roles and follow applicable law. AU-02 defines which event types to log, with the reasons they suffice for investigating incidents, and AU-12 lets defined roles choose what each component logs, with AU-12(03) letting authorised staff change the logging. AU-11 keeps audit records for a set period to support investigations and meet retention rules, and AU-16 sets methods for passing audit information to outside organisations, such as customers. AU-08 has time stamps generated from internal clocks in Coordinated Universal Time or with a stated offset, and SC-45 synchronises system clocks, with SC-45(01) and SC-45(02) using a primary and a secondary authoritative time source. SI-04 monitors the system against defined objectives and calls for a legal opinion on that monitoring.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to state the purpose of each log and the criteria that make a time source reliable. Add both to the AU-01 procedures.

clauses.title: Using derived and account data only to run the service
clauses.rationale: AU-01 and PT-01 give documented policies with procedures for audit records and for processing personal data, which govern how derived and account data are handled. PT-03 documents the purposes for processing personal data and limits processing to purposes compatible with them, which keeps use to running the service. AU-09 protects audit information against unauthorised access and tampering, AU-11 keeps records for a set period, and SI-12(03) disposes of information under SI-12 once the retention period ends. AU-03(03) limits the personal data in audit records, and SI-19 removes defined personal data elements from datasets and checks how well the de-identification works. AU-16 coordinates audit information with outside organisations, and AU-16(02) covers sharing it, which supports giving log data to customers under the contract.
clauses.gaps: C5 limits derived data to running the service and asks the provider to name in customer contracts every purpose for collecting it, beyond those common to all cloud services. Extend the PT-03 purpose limits to all derived data, personal or anonymous, and add the purposes to the contracts. The additional criteria bring log data into regulatory compliance assessments.

clauses.title: Technical limits on who sees logs and how long they stay
clauses.rationale: AU-09 protects audit information and logging tools from unauthorised access and tampering, and AU-09(04) gives access only to a subset of privileged users. AU-11 keeps audit records for the set period. SI-12 manages and retains information as laws and operational needs require, and SI-12(03) disposes of it once the retention period ends.

clauses.title: Central security event analysis linked to incident response
clauses.rationale: AU-06 reviews and analyses audit records for unusual activity, and AU-06(01), AU-06(03), AU-06(04) and AU-06(05) automate that review and bring records from many sources together for central, integrated analysis. AU-12(02) compiles the audit trail in a standard format under AU-12, which standardises log data. SI-04 monitors for attacks and analyses detected events, with SI-04(02) for real-time analysis, SI-04(05) for system alerts, SI-04(07) for automated response to suspicious events and SI-04(09) for testing the monitoring tools. IR-04(01) and IR-04(04) automate incident handling under IR-04 and correlate incident information, which links detected events to incident response.
clauses.gaps: The additional criteria ask the provider to choose the assets on which it checks event detection according to their classification. Base the SI-04(09) tests on that classification.

clauses.title: Storing logs centrally in tamper-proof form
clauses.rationale: AU-11 keeps audit records for a set period to support investigations. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised change and deletion, and AU-09(01) and AU-09(03) add write-once media and cryptographic protection, which keeps logs unchangeable. AU-06(04) brings records from many components together for central review under AU-06. IA-03 authenticates defined devices before a connection is made, and SC-08(01) encrypts log transfers under SC-08. SI-12 manages the retention of information, and SI-12(03) disposes of logs once the retention period ends.
clauses.gaps: C5 also allows a dedicated out-of-band administration network in place of encrypting log transfers. Where the provider uses one, document the network and how it protects the logs.

clauses.title: Logs that trace each access and support forensic work
clauses.rationale: AU-03 has each audit record show the type, time, place, source and outcome of the event and who was involved, which identifies user access. AU-08 dates each record from internal clocks in Coordinated Universal Time, and SC-45 keeps clocks in step across systems. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised change and deletion, and AU-10 gives irrefutable evidence of defined actions, with AU-10(03) keeping the chain of custody. IR-04(12) adds forensic analysis to the incident handling of IR-04, and AU-16(02) shares audit information with outside organisations under AU-16, which lets the provider give customers their logs.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the logs to identify access at the level of each tenant. Capture the state of hardware and network traffic during a security event, and show that copies of evidence match the originals. Add both to the IR-04 forensic procedures.

clauses.title: Multi-factor access to logging systems and controlled changes
clauses.rationale: AU-09 protects audit information and logging tools from unauthorised access, and AU-09(04) limits access to a subset of privileged users. IA-02 identifies and authenticates each user uniquely, and IA-02(01) and IA-02(02) require multi-factor authentication for privileged and other accounts. CM-03 runs configuration changes through review and approval, which governs changes to the logging set-up.

clauses.title: Alerts when logging or monitoring tools fail
clauses.rationale: AU-05 alerts defined roles within a set time when audit logging fails and takes further defined actions. AU-05(02) sends the alerts in real time and AU-05(05) keeps an alternate logging capability. SI-06 verifies that defined security functions work and alerts staff when a check fails, which shows whether the monitoring tools are running. AU-09 protects audit information and logging tools from unauthorised access and tampering, and AU-09(02) stores records on separate physical systems.
clauses.gaps: The additional criteria ask for the logging and monitoring platform to keep working when a single component fails. Find its single points of failure and remove them through redundancy.

clauses.title: Rules for finding and fixing vulnerabilities on time
clauses.rationale: RA-01 and SI-01 give documented and shared policies with procedures for risk assessment and for system integrity, which hold the vulnerability rules. RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities on a set cycle and when new ones are reported, using standards to measure their impact, and remediates them within response times set by risk. It also shares what it finds with defined roles. CA-08 runs penetration tests on a set cycle, and SI-02 corrects flaws and installs security updates within a set time of their release, with SI-02(03) setting benchmarks for the time to remediate.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks work on critical vulnerabilities to start promptly, even out of hours, and on high ones within one working day. Set those times in RA-05. C5 also asks for documented, expert-led use of any AI-based scanning tools, and for vulnerability and patch information in widely used machine-readable formats such as CSAF or VEX.

clauses.title: How incidents and crashes are handled and recorded
clauses.rationale: IR-01 gives a documented and shared incident response policy with procedures. IR-08 has an incident response plan that defines reportable incidents and assigns responsibility for response, which covers classification and escalation. AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access, which keeps crash files to authorised staff. SC-08 and SC-28 protect the confidentiality and integrity of crash files in transit and at rest, with SC-08(01) and SC-28(01) using cryptography. SI-12 manages and retains information as requirements dictate, and SI-12(03) disposes of crash files once their retention period ends.
clauses.gaps: C5 covers operational incidents and crashes as well as security ones, including standard fixes for known issues and the criteria for treating a crash as an incident. Extend the IR-01 procedures to them and name the knowledge sources the team draws on. Add safeguards that keep sensitive data out of crash files.

clauses.title: Recording and resolving incidents as the procedures set out
clauses.rationale: IR-04 gives an incident handling capability, in line with the incident response plan, that covers preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery. IR-05 tracks and documents each incident, which gives the record C5 asks for.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to classify and prioritise every incident, including purely operational ones. Apply IR-04 handling and IR-05 records to those incidents as well.

clauses.title: Spotting and fixing crashes of components or the service
clauses.rationale: CP-10 recovers and rebuilds the system to a known state after a disruption or failure, which restores service after a crash. IR-04 handles crashes treated as incidents through detection, analysis, containment and recovery, and IR-05 tracks and documents them.
clauses.gaps: C5 treats crashes as a class of their own, apart from security incidents. Set up a process that identifies and records every crash, from a single component up to the whole service, and link it to CP-10 recovery.

clauses.title: Regular, risk-based penetration testing of the service
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests on defined components on a set cycle, and CA-08(01) uses an independent agent or team. CA-01 gives the documented assessment policy and procedures, which hold the testing framework. SA-11 has developers test and evaluate the system at every stage after design, and SA-11(05) and SA-11(02) add penetration testing before launch and threat modelling. RA-05 measures vulnerability impact against standards and remediates within set response times, and RA-05(08) reviews historic audit logs to see whether a flaw was exploited before it was found. SI-02 corrects flaws, and SI-02(07) analyses their root cause.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the testing framework to set the qualifications testers need. Plan the tests so that every relevant component is tested at least once in three years. The additional criteria also ask for a yearly review of how effective the tests are.

clauses.title: Measuring how well vulnerability and incident handling works
clauses.rationale: PM-06 has the provider track and report measures of security performance, which can show how well the vulnerability and incident procedures work. IR-08 has the incident response plan provide metrics for the response capability. IR-03 tests how effective the response capability is on a set cycle, and IR-03(03) uses the test results to improve the process.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks responsible staff to evaluate the results in writing at least once a quarter, to start improvements and check that they work. Set metrics for the vulnerability procedures alongside the IR-08 incident metrics.

clauses.title: Keeping affected customers informed during incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-07 provides an incident response support resource that gives users of the system advice and help with handling and reporting incidents, which lets customers take part in resolving them. The resource is part of the provider's own incident response capability.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to update affected customers on an incident's status at regular intervals and to tell them what was done once it is resolved. Write both into the customer contracts. The additional criterion adds a contract term for customers to confirm, within a set time, that the fix dealt with the root cause.

clauses.title: Scanning for known vulnerabilities at least monthly
clauses.rationale: RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities on a set cycle and when new ones are reported, and scores their impact against standards. It remediates them within set response times, and RA-05(02) keeps the list of vulnerabilities to scan for up to date. SI-02 corrects flaws and installs security updates within a set time, and SI-02(03) measures how long remediation takes. SI-04 monitors for attacks against defined objectives and adjusts monitoring when risk changes, which lets scan results sharpen the detection of known flaws being exploited.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for scans at least once a month, or daily under the additional criteria. Set that frequency in RA-05, and feed each scan's results into the rules of the security event management system so they detect active exploitation of known vulnerabilities.

clauses.title: Hardening production components to industry benchmarks
clauses.rationale: CM-06 sets configuration settings in the most restrictive mode that operations allow, based on common secure configurations, and monitors changes to them. CM-06(01) verifies the settings automatically and CM-06(02) responds to unauthorised changes. CM-07 limits each system to essential capabilities and restricts unneeded functions, ports, protocols and services. CM-02 keeps a documented baseline configuration under configuration control, and CM-02(03) retains earlier versions, which records image configurations. SI-07 uses integrity verification tools to detect unauthorised changes to defined software and information, which shows whether components stay hardened.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to check each immutable image against the hardening specification when the image is created. Add that check to the image build process.

clauses.title: Rules for timely, tested patching
clauses.rationale: SI-01 and CM-01 give documented and shared policies with procedures for system integrity and configuration management, which hold the patch rules and tie them to change management. SI-02 tests updates for effectiveness and side effects before installation and installs security updates within a set time. It also builds flaw remediation into configuration management, with SI-02(04) adding automated patch management tools. CM-03 runs changes through review and approval, CM-03(02) tests and validates them first, and CM-04(01) analyses them in a separate test environment under CM-04. CM-02(03) retains earlier configurations under CM-02, which supports rolling back, and RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities, which shows whether a patch removed them.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for patches to be scheduled in maintenance windows where that limits disruption. Add that to the SI-01 procedures. The additional criterion also asks for an exception process for patches that need manual work.

clauses.title: Deploying patches through change control
clauses.rationale: SI-02 installs security-relevant software and firmware updates within a set time of their release, after testing them. SI-02(04) and SI-02(05) support deployment with automated patch management tools and automatic updates. CM-03 implements approved changes and keeps records of them, which runs patch deployment through change control.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the deployment to follow every measure in the patch policy, such as scheduling patches in maintenance windows. Check that the SI-02 and CM-03 processes apply them.

clauses.title: Keeping third-party and open-source libraries up to date
clauses.rationale: RA-05 monitors and scans the system and hosted applications for vulnerabilities on a set cycle and when new ones are reported, which finds known flaws in libraries. CM-04 analyses each change for its security impact before it is made, which judges the effect of library updates. SI-02 tests updates and installs security updates within a set time, which covers updating third-party and open-source libraries.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to track the updates available for third-party and open-source libraries, as well as their known vulnerabilities. Add that tracking to the RA-05 monitoring.

clauses.title: Rules for keeping each customer's data apart
clauses.rationale: SC-01 gives a documented and shared system and communications protection policy with procedures, which holds the separation rules. PL-08 has the provider develop security architectures that describe the requirements and approach for protecting its information, which can set out the separation measures for each protection goal. SC-04 prevents unauthorised and unintended transfer of information through shared system resources, which is the aim of separating customers' data.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a documented cloud layer model with the separation measures for each layer, sorted by protection goal and by whether they prevent, detect or react. Base the measures on a risk assessment, and monitor them so that deviations trigger action. Record this in the PL-08 architecture.

clauses.title: Strict separation of customer data on shared resources
clauses.rationale: SC-04 prevents unauthorised and unintended transfer of information through shared system resources. SC-32 partitions the system into components in separate physical or logical domains, and SC-50 enforces separation in software between defined security domains, such as tenants. SC-39 keeps a separate execution domain for each process, and SC-28(01) protects stored information with cryptography under SC-28, which supports cryptographic separation of customer data. RA-03 reviews the risk assessment on a set cycle and updates it after significant changes, such as changes to the architecture.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for measures that detect and respond to breaches of separation as well as prevent them. Add those measures, tied to the documented separation approach.

clauses.title: Policy for protecting data in use with trusted hardware
clauses.rationale: SC-01 gives a documented and shared system and communications protection policy with procedures, which can hold the confidential computing rules. SC-49 enforces separation between defined security domains in hardware, which is how trusted execution environments shield data in use. SC-12 manages cryptographic keys under defined rules for their generation, distribution, storage, access and destruction, and SC-13 implements the types of cryptography each use requires. SA-05 gives customers documentation of the security functions open to them and how to use them, which tells them about the confidential computing features.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to state which parts of the stack each confidential computing technology protects and which suppliers are involved. C5 also asks that customer data and its keys stay beyond the reach of the provider and of any other unauthorised party. Add both to the SC-01 policy, and offer remote attestation of the protected environments.

clauses.title: Letting customers verify trusted execution remotely
clauses.rationale: SI-07 uses integrity verification tools to detect unauthorised changes to defined software and firmware. SI-07(06) adds cryptographic protection and SI-07(09) verifies the boot process, which roots the checks in cryptography and trusted components. SA-05 gives customers documentation of the security functions open to them and how to use them, which documents the attestation features and levels.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to offer customers remote attestation of the protection of data in use, rooted in trusted hardware and software. Provide an interface through which customers can check the integrity of the attestation.

clauses.title: Securing containers and images across their life cycle
clauses.rationale: CM-01 gives a documented configuration management policy with procedures for the container life cycle, and CM-02 keeps baseline configurations under control, which governs how images are built and validated. CM-03 runs changes to containers and images through review and approval, CM-06 and CM-07 harden them with restrictive settings and only essential services, and CM-08 inventories them. CM-14 allows installation only of components whose signature is verified against an approved certificate, which enforces signed images, and RA-05 scans hosted applications, images included, for vulnerabilities. AU-02 sets the events to log along the life cycle, SI-04 monitors for attacks and analyses anomalies, and SI-03 adds malware protection where containers need it. AC-03 enforces approved access to container hosts, SC-04 keeps customer data apart on shared resources, and SC-08 and SC-28 protect data in transit and at rest.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to cover how images are stored and retrieved, and to keep the image signing key in secure storage. Add both to the CM-01 procedures for containers.

clauses.title: Putting the container rules into practice
clauses.rationale: CM-02 keeps the baseline configuration of images current and under control, and CM-03 implements only approved changes to containers and images. CM-06 applies restrictive configuration settings and CM-07 limits containers to essential services, with CM-07(06) confining them to environments with limited privileges. CM-14 allows installation only of components whose signature is verified against an approved certificate, CM-08 keeps running containers in the inventory, and RA-05 scans images for vulnerabilities. AC-03 enforces approved access to container hosts, SC-04 keeps customer data apart on shared resources, and SC-08 and SC-28 protect data in transit and at rest. SI-03 protects containers from malware where needed, and SI-04 monitors their networks and behaviour for attacks and anomalies.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to put the whole container policy into practice, including how it stores and retrieves images and how it keeps the image signing key safe. Build both into the container processes.

clauses.title: Identity and access policy with a role-based framework
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and IA-01 have the provider document and share policies and procedures for access control and for identification and authentication. AC-02 sets account types, approvals, the privileges of each account and regular reviews, which supports a list of each identity's rights, and AC-02(02), AC-02(03) and AC-02(07) cover emergency, inactive and privileged accounts. AC-03(07) enforces access through roles and AC-06 grants only the access each task needs, while AC-05 documents the duties to keep apart. IA-02 identifies each user uniquely and IA-04 assigns identifiers only with approval, and IA-02(01) adds multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts. AC-17 sets the rules and approval for each type of remote access, and AU-06 reviews audit records for unusual activity at a frequency the provider sets.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to cover access across geographic boundaries and the steps to take when an identity may be compromised, such as disabling it. Add both to the AC-01 policy. Set the AU-06 review of access logs to at least monthly.

clauses.title: Granting and changing identities, with break-glass rules
clauses.rationale: AC-02 requires approval of account requests and creates, modifies, disables and removes accounts by criteria the provider sets. It also reviews accounts at a set frequency, which checks the permissions in place, and AC-02(02) manages temporary and emergency accounts, such as break-glass accounts. AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access, so only authorised staff reach the provider's data and system functions. IA-04 requires approval from set roles before an identifier goes to a person, group, role, service or device, which covers system components as well as people.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for specific rules on the safe use of break-glass accounts, beyond the automatic handling in AC-02(02). Write those rules into the account management procedures.

clauses.title: Risk-based locking of identities and watch for stolen credentials
clauses.rationale: AC-02(03) disables accounts after a set period of inactivity, AC-02(12) watches accounts for atypical use and AC-02(13) disables the accounts of high-risk individuals. AC-07 locks an account or node after a set number of failed logon attempts, which answers brute force attacks. IA-05 sets procedures for lost or compromised authenticators and for revoking them, and AU-13 watches open sources for signs that organisational information, such as credentials, has leaked. CP-13 brings in alternative security mechanisms when the primary means is unavailable or compromised, which serves as the exception path when every managing identity may be compromised. CA-02 assesses whether these controls work as intended, and CA-05 plans the remediation of the weaknesses found.
clauses.gaps: C5 bases the procedure on the types of data each identity can reach. Set the locking and withdrawal parameters by that data, and exempt the identities kept for emergency recovery from automatic locking.

clauses.title: Adjusting or removing access when duties or tasks change
clauses.rationale: AC-02 notifies account managers within set periods when users are transferred or their need to know changes, and modifies or removes accounts to match. AC-02(02) manages temporary accounts automatically, which suits time-limited access during a role change. PS-05 reviews the need for access when staff move to another role and modifies their authorisations to match. PS-04 disables system access within a set period when employment ends and revokes the person's credentials. PS-07 requires external providers to report transfers and terminations of their staff who hold credentials or privileges.
clauses.gaps: C5 sets deadlines of 48 hours for privileged rights and 14 days for all other rights. Use them as the periods in AC-02, PS-04 and PS-05, and repeat the granting procedure after each revocation. Record an approval and an end date for any temporary access given during a role change.

clauses.title: Yearly access review and clean-up of orphaned resources
clauses.rationale: AC-02 reviews accounts against the account management rules at a set frequency and modifies or removes accounts to match. AC-06(07) reviews user privileges at a set frequency to confirm they are still needed. CM-08 keeps an accurate inventory of system components, and CM-08(04) records who is accountable for each one, which reveals any orphaned resources.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for each deviation the review finds to be fixed within seven days. Set that deadline in the review procedure. When an identity is revoked, reassign or securely delete every production resource it owned.

clauses.title: Managing and monitoring privileged access
clauses.rationale: AC-02(07) runs privileged accounts under a role-based scheme and watches privileged role assignments. AC-06 limits access to what tasks need, AC-06(05) keeps privileged accounts to set personnel and AC-06(09) logs the use of privileged functions. AU-12 generates the audit records, AU-06(01) brings automated processes into their review, and SI-04(20) adds monitoring of privileged users, with SI-04(05) raising alerts. IA-02(01) requires multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts, and IA-02(05) requires individual sign-in before a shared account is used. PS-08 applies a formal sanctions process to people who break security policies.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication with domain binding, such as FIDO2 keys, for privileged users. It also asks for a list of the people responsible for each non-human identity, reviewed every six months, and for a privileged access management tool with just-in-time elevation. Build these into the IA-02 and AC-02 arrangements.

clauses.title: Tenant separation and notice of provider access to customer data
clauses.rationale: SC-32 places system components in separate physical or logical domains, SC-07(21) isolates set components, and SC-04 prevents unintended transfer of information through shared resources, which keeps customers apart. SC-03 isolates security functions from other functions, which keeps the components that manage access apart from those that store data. SC-02 separates user functions from system management, which serves separate interfaces for customer administrators and end users. PS-03 screens staff before they get access, and MA-05 has authorised, competent staff supervise the maintenance work of those who lack the required authorisations. For supervised access, AC-03(02) requires a second person to approve set actions, AU-14 lets set roles view or record a user session and AU-12 generates the audit records. IA-02 and IA-03 authenticate the supervised person and their device, and AC-04 enforces approved information flows, which can block data heading to that device.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to tell customers within 72 hours when its staff read or write their data, with the cause, time, place and scope of the access. It also asks for prior customer consent and for contracts that list every case where the provider can see unencrypted data. Add these terms to the customer contract and the access procedure.

clauses.title: Authentication of staff and components, with MFA and lockout
clauses.rationale: IA-02 uniquely identifies and authenticates staff, IA-02(01) and IA-02(02) require multi-factor authentication for privileged and other accounts, and IA-02(05) requires individual sign-in before a shared account is used. IA-03 authenticates devices before they connect, and IA-09 authenticates system services and applications before they communicate, which covers components in automated processes.
