IA-01 documents and shares the authentication policy, and IA-05 sets the strength, first issue, regular change and protection of authenticators, with procedures for lost or compromised ones. RA-03 assesses threats and vulnerabilities, which grounds the authentication requirements and the judgement of when a mechanism is out of date, and SA-22 replaces components once their supplier stops supporting them. AC-07 locks an account after a set number of failed logon attempts.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for multi-factor authentication for automated processes as well as for people, so extend the rule to service identities. Add the ageing of authentication mechanisms to the RA-03 risk assessment and plan their replacement from its results.

clauses.title: Safe handling of passwords and other credentials
clauses.rationale: IA-05 verifies who receives an authenticator when it is first issued and protects authenticator content from disclosure and change. IA-05(01) sets rules for password-based authentication, IA-05(06) protects authenticators to the level of the information they unlock and IA-05(18) covers password managers. AC-09(03) notifies users of changes to their account, such as a password reset, and SC-13 applies the types of cryptography set for each use, such as hashing stored passwords. PL-04 gives users rules on their security duties and collects a documented acknowledgement, and AT-02 trains them, with AT-02(03) on social engineering such as phishing.
clauses.gaps: C5 limits an initial password to 14 days and a reset procedure to 24 hours. Set both limits in IA-05. Assess any departure from the password rules for risk and apply the measures that follow from it.

clauses.title: Cryptography policy and post-quantum strategy
clauses.rationale: SC-01 has the provider document and share a system and communications protection policy with procedures, which holds the cryptography rules, and review it at set intervals. SC-13 sets the types of cryptography for each use, which covers encryption, hashing, signatures and protocols. SC-12 sets the key management requirements for generation, distribution, storage, access and destruction, and CM-03(06) brings cryptographic mechanisms under change control. RA-03 assesses threats and vulnerabilities, which is where deviations and quantum risks are weighed, and PM-15 keeps contact with security groups to stay current with recommended practices and technologies.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for crypto-agility and for a check of the policy against BSI TR-02102 or NIST guidance such as FIPS 140. Cover crypto-agility in the SC-01 policy and add the check to its review. For the optional post-quantum strategy, keep a ranked inventory of the mechanisms in use and a transition plan with hybrid schemes and trigger events.

clauses.title: Assessing and recording changes to cryptographic systems
clauses.rationale: CM-04 analyses each change for its possible security and privacy impact before it is made. CM-03 reviews proposed changes with that analysis in view, documents the decisions and keeps records of the changes, and CM-03(06) brings cryptographic mechanisms under this control, so cryptographic changes stay traceable. AT-03 gives role-based training to set roles at a set frequency and when system changes call for it, which reaches the staff who run cryptographic systems.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the impact analysis to weigh disruption to customer workloads along with cost and benefit. Tell customers how a cryptographic change may affect their own setups before it takes effect.

clauses.title: Yearly and incident-driven audits of cryptographic practice
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses controls at a set frequency to find out whether they are implemented correctly and work as intended, which covers audits of encryption, authentication and key management. CA-05 keeps a plan of action that records the remediation planned for weaknesses found, which drives the updates the review calls for.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a review at least once a year and straight after any security incident that involves cryptographic components. Set both triggers for CA-02, and have each review compare the practices with the current state of the art.

clauses.title: Encrypting and authenticating data in transit
clauses.rationale: SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit, and SC-08(01) does so with cryptography, which covers customer data sent over public networks. SC-13 sets the types of cryptography for each use, and SC-23 protects the authenticity of communication sessions. AC-17 sets connection requirements for each type of remote access, and AC-17(02) encrypts remote sessions to protect them. IA-02 authenticates the staff who connect to production.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for encryption that matches the state of the art. Choose current algorithms and protocol settings in SC-13 and keep them under review.

clauses.title: Encrypting stored customer data and keeping keys with the customer
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protects set information at rest, and SC-28(01) does so with cryptography, which covers customer data in storage. SC-13 sets the types of cryptography for that use, and SC-12 sets the rules for key storage and access, which can limit who reaches the keys. SC-04 prevents unintended transfer of information through shared resources, which supports the optional rule that customer data stays unrecoverable when resources are reallocated. CA-02 assesses at a set frequency whether controls work as intended, which covers testing the controls around a master key.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the keys to be held by the customer alone, with any provider access handled as a set exception. Agree the key procedures and their exceptions with each customer, and tell customers of any change that could weaken the protection of their data.

clauses.title: Creating keys from secure random bit generators
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys under set requirements that include key generation, and SC-12(02) and SC-12(03) cover symmetric and asymmetric keys. SC-13 sets the types of cryptography for each use, which is where the provider can require approved random bit generators.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for keys to come from secure random bit generators, or from keys made that way. Write this rule into the SC-12 key generation requirements.

clauses.title: Scheduled key rotation and notice when the provider skips it
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys under requirements the provider sets for their generation, distribution, storage, access and destruction. Those requirements are the place for a rotation schedule that follows the cryptography policy.
clauses.gaps: SC-12 leaves rotation to the provider's own key requirements. Add a rotation schedule to them, in line with the cryptography policy. When a risk assessment leads the provider to skip rotation, tell the affected customers.

clauses.title: Issuing and obtaining certificates securely
clauses.rationale: SC-17 issues public key certificates under a set certificate policy or obtains them from an approved provider, and keeps only approved trust anchors in the trust stores. IA-05 verifies the identity of the person, service or device that receives an authenticator when it is first issued, and IA-05(02) covers public key-based authentication. SC-12(03) covers the management of asymmetric keys, which protects the keys behind the certificates.

clauses.title: Issuing keys to verified holders with set validity dates
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets the requirements for key distribution and access, which govern how keys are provisioned and activated. IA-05 verifies the identity of whoever receives an authenticator when it is first issued, which applies to keys that act as authenticators.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for an authorisation check before each key is activated, and for every key to carry activation and deactivation dates. Add both to the SC-12 key requirements.

clauses.title: Protected key stores separate from the application layer
clauses.rationale: SC-03 isolates security functions from other functions, which keeps the key management system apart from the application and middleware layers. SC-12 sets the requirements for key storage and access, which define how authorised users reach the keys. SC-28(03) provides protected storage for cryptographic keys, which matches the optional hardware or software security module.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to decide where keys may reside, to meet legal and contract terms. Record the permitted locations in the SC-12 requirements and enforce them.

clauses.title: Archiving keys safely for later recovery
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets requirements for key storage, access and destruction, and SC-12(01) keeps information available when keys are lost, which supports recovery through archived keys. AC-06 allows only the access each task needs, which limits archived keys to authorised staff. AU-02 names the events to log, such as storing and recovering an archived key, and AU-12 generates the audit records for them.
clauses.gaps: C5 limits how long archived keys are kept. Set a retention period in the SC-12 requirements and destroy keys securely when it ends.

clauses.title: Overseeing changes in key state, such as suspension
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys under requirements the provider sets for each stage of a key's life, from generation to destruction. Those requirements are where rules for suspending and reactivating keys can sit.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for oversight and approval of each change in a key's state, including moves into and out of suspension. Define these states and the approval step in the SC-12 key requirements.

clauses.title: Limiting compromised keys and telling affected customers
clauses.rationale: IA-05 sets procedures for lost or compromised authenticators and for revoking them, which covers keys used to authenticate. SC-12 manages keys under set requirements for access and destruction, which can confine a compromised key to decryption or signature checks.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for compromised keys to serve only for decryption or signature checks, under controlled conditions. Write this into the SC-12 requirements. Tell affected customers promptly when their keys are compromised and withdrawn from encryption and signing.

clauses.title: Retiring keys and logging their destruction
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets requirements for key destruction, which is where the rules for expired and deactivated keys belong. AU-02 names the event types to log, such as deactivating or destroying a key, and AU-12 generates the audit records for them, which leaves an audit trail.
clauses.gaps: C5 limits expired keys to decryption and signature checks, and asks for key metadata to be kept for audit after a key is destroyed. Add both rules to the SC-12 requirements.

clauses.title: Safe use of pre-shared keys and wildcard certificates
clauses.rationale: SC-12(02) covers the management of symmetric keys, which include pre-shared keys. SC-17 issues public key certificates under a set certificate policy, which can set rules for wildcard certificates.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for dedicated procedures for pre-shared keys and wildcard certificates. Add them to the key management requirements and the certificate policy, and state where each may be used.

clauses.title: Key backup or redundancy to keep key services running
clauses.rationale: CP-09 backs up system-level information and protects the backup copies, which covers secure backups of key material. SC-12(01) keeps information available when keys are lost, which supports procedures to recover lost or corrupted keys.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to weigh backups of HSM key material against redundant HSMs, including how exposed the keys would be if the provider lost control of them. Document the choice and review the chosen measure for effectiveness and against contract and legal terms.

clauses.title: Tracking keys through their lives, with full records
clauses.rationale: SC-12 manages keys under set requirements from generation through distribution, storage and access to destruction, which spans the life of a key. AU-02 names the events to log, such as each change in a key's status, and AU-12 generates the audit records that build each key's history.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a full record of each key, apart from ephemeral keys, from creation to destruction, with every change of status. Keep this record in the key management system as well as in the event log.

clauses.title: Using an outside key management service securely
clauses.rationale: SA-04 puts security assurance requirements into the acquisition contract, and SA-04(07) calls for products evaluated against approved protection profiles, which supports recognised certifications. SA-09 requires whoever runs the external service to meet the provider's security requirements, and the provider monitors that compliance. AC-03 enforces approved authorisations, so only authorised users and systems reach the keys, and SC-12 sets the key management requirements, which is where rotation and renewal belong. AU-02 names each access to and operation on the external system as an event to log, AU-12 generates the records and AU-06 reviews them for unusual activity. RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities at a set frequency, and SI-02 installs security updates within a set time.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a secure integration of the external key management system into the cloud infrastructure. Design and test that integration to protect the keys it handles.

clauses.title: Protecting keys that customers bring and manage
clauses.rationale: SC-12 sets requirements for key distribution, storage and access, which can cover bringing customer-generated keys into the environment. AC-03 enforces approved authorisations, so only authorised users reach customer-managed keys. AU-02 names all activity on those keys as events to log, and AU-12 generates the audit records.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for specific steps to import keys that customers generate themselves. Add a bring-your-own-key procedure to the SC-12 requirements.

clauses.title: Layered defences that detect and stop network attacks
clauses.rationale: SI-04 monitors the system for attacks, signs of attack and unauthorised connections, and SI-04(04) and SI-04(11) watch inbound and outbound traffic for unusual patterns. PL-08(01) builds the security architecture in layers, SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at managed interfaces, and SC-05 protects against or limits denial-of-service events such as DDoS. SI-10 checks the validity of inputs, and SI-10(06) prevents injection of untrusted data. IA-03 authenticates devices before they connect, which keeps unknown devices off the network, and AU-06(03) and AU-06(04) correlate audit records and analyse them centrally, as a SIEM does. SC-01 and SI-01 document the policies and procedures that hold these safeguards.
clauses.gaps: C5 names attacks on IoT devices and DNS tunnelling among the threats to cover. Add them to the SI-04 monitoring objectives, and choose the safeguards from the results of a risk assessment.

clauses.title: Network zoning and permitted connections inside the provider
clauses.rationale: SC-07 places public components in separate subnetworks and connects to external networks only through managed interfaces arranged under the security architecture, and SC-07(29) isolates functions in separate subnets, which supports separate management traffic. AC-04 enforces approved information flows within the system and between connected systems, which sets the permitted communication relationships. CM-07 restricts functions, ports, protocols and services to those allowed. CA-09 authorises internal connections and documents the security requirements of each, which covers communication across partitions. AC-17 and AC-18 set connection requirements for remote and wireless access, which covers VPN and Wi-Fi in office networks.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the requirements to say when customers are kept apart logically and when physically. Record those cases in the security architecture behind SC-07.

clauses.title: Trusted and untrusted zones, with yearly network reviews
clauses.rationale: SC-07 places public components in separate subnetworks and monitors and controls traffic at managed interfaces, which gives trusted and untrusted zones and a DMZ. SI-04 watches for unauthorised local, network and remote connections. CM-06 sets, applies and monitors configuration settings, which keeps the network configuration in line with the requirements, and CA-09 reviews the continued need for each internal connection at a set frequency. CM-07(01) reviews functions, ports, protocols and services at a set frequency to find those that are unnecessary or insecure. RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance, and CA-05 tracks the planned remediation.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a recorded justification of the compensating measures wherever an insecure protocol stays in use. Include it in the CM-07(01) review.

clauses.title: Security gateways at each network boundary
clauses.rationale: SC-07 connects to external networks only through managed interfaces made of boundary protection devices, which places a security gateway at each network perimeter. AC-04 enforces approved authorisations for information flows between connected systems, which governs access from one network to another.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for each approval of access across networks to rest on a security assessment of the customers' requirements. Add that assessment to the AC-04 flow policies, and make the gateways redundant and highly available if you adopt the sharper optional criterion.

clauses.title: Separate administration networks protected by MFA
clauses.rationale: SC-07(29) uses separate subnets to isolate functions, and SC-07(15) routes networked privileged access through a dedicated managed interface, which gives separate networks for administration and for workload orchestration. SC-02 separates system management functions, such as management consoles, from user functions. IA-02(01) requires multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts, which protects access to the administration networks. SC-08(01) protects transmitted information with cryptography, which covers administration traffic that shares a physical network.

clauses.title: Keeping each customer's traffic apart on shared networks
clauses.rationale: AC-04(21) separates information flows by physical or logical means, which keeps each customer's traffic apart at network level. SC-07 places public components in separate subnetworks, and SC-07(21) isolates set system components. SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit, and SC-08(01) adds cryptography, which is the encryption option C5 offers for IaaS and PaaS.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a documented framework that sets out how customer traffic is kept apart on shared networks. Write it and link it to the AC-04 flow policies.

clauses.title: Current network maps and where customer data is kept
clauses.rationale: PL-02 builds a security plan that defines the system's components and describes its environment and its connections to other systems, and reviews the plan at a set frequency. CA-09 documents each internal connection, including the nature of the information exchanged, which records the data flows between subnets and components. CM-12 documents where set information is processed and stored and on which components, which shows where customer data sits. CM-08 keeps an accurate inventory of system components, which ties the network picture to the asset inventory.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for network documentation that shows how subnets are allocated and zoned and how the network links to outside networks. Review it at least once a year and correct promptly any deviation the review finds.

clauses.title: Policy and safeguards for moving data securely
clauses.rationale: SC-01 has the provider document and share a system and communications protection policy with procedures, which holds the rules for data transmission. SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit, which guards against interception and tampering, and SC-13 sets the cryptography for each use. SI-03 places malicious code protection at system entry and exit points. CA-02 assesses the controls at a set frequency, which covers the regular review of the transmission safeguards.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the transmission policy to refer to the asset classification and labelling scheme. Add that link in the SC-01 policy, and review the safeguards after each significant change to the service as well as on the CA-02 cycle.

clauses.title: Secure, documented interfaces for customer systems and data export
clauses.rationale: SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of data in transit, and SC-08(01) uses cryptography for interface traffic over untrusted networks. IA-08 identifies and authenticates users and processes from outside the organisation, and IA-08(02) accepts external authenticators, which supports customer identity providers. SI-07 uses integrity verification tools to detect unauthorised changes to set information, and CP-09 backs up user-level and system-level information and protects the backups. SA-05 provides user documentation on functions and ways of interacting with the system, which keeps customers informed about protocols and formats. SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at external managed interfaces, which supports an application firewall in front of customer administration interfaces.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for standard data formats and processing standards that let other systems work with the data. It also asks the provider to give customers the technical means to extract their data, or an extraction service where self-service is impractical. Build both into the service and describe them in the customer documentation.

clauses.title: Contract terms for returning customer data at exit
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 covers contracts only from the buyer's side, as when an organisation acquires a service. C5 asks for terms the provider gives its own customers on handing back their data when the contract ends, covering format, delivery, time frames, the deletion date and ownership of the data. Write these terms into the customer contract.

clauses.title: Deleting customer data at contract end, with proof
clauses.rationale: MP-06 sanitises media before disposal, release or reuse with mechanisms whose strength matches the classification of the information, which resists forensic recovery. MP-06(01) reviews, tracks, documents and verifies the sanitisation, which gives a record of it. SI-12 manages and retains information in line with laws and other requirements, and SI-12(03) disposes of information when its retention period ends.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for deletion that follows the customer contract and for proof of deletion the customer can obtain. Tie the MP-06 procedures to the contract terms and give each customer a record that its data was deleted.

clauses.title: Secure development rules across the whole service life cycle
clauses.rationale: SA-01 has the provider document and share a system and services acquisition policy with procedures, which holds the rules for secure development and procurement. SA-03 runs a development life cycle that builds in security and integrates risk management. SA-08 applies security engineering principles from specification to modification, which is security by design, and SA-08(33) on minimisation supports keeping provider access to customer data low. SA-15 requires a documented development process that addresses security and names its standards and tools, and SA-11 has the developer test, produce evidence and fix the flaws found. SA-04(07) calls for products evaluated against approved protection profiles, which matches the optional preference for certified products.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a risk assessment whenever an uncertified product is bought in place of an available certified one. Add this step to the SA-04 acquisition procedure, and cover secure deployment through continuous delivery in the development rules.

clauses.title: Contract terms and risk checks for outsourced development
clauses.rationale: SA-04 puts security requirements, assurance requirements and acceptance criteria into the contract with the developer. SA-15 requires the developer to follow a documented process that addresses security and names its standards and tools. SA-11 has the developer test the work, produce evidence of the results and fix the flaws found, which gives proof of checks for known vulnerabilities. SR-06 assesses the supply chain risks of contractors and of what they provide, which covers the risk assessment before outsourcing. SA-09 requires external providers to meet the provider's security requirements and monitors their compliance, which supports oversight of the outsourced work.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider's own staff to run the tests that decide whether a change containing outsourced work may be deployed. Assign those tests to internal staff in the release procedure.

clauses.title: Change management policy for the service's components
clauses.rationale: CM-01 has the provider document and share a configuration management policy with procedures, which holds the change rules, and CM-09 sets out roles, responsibilities and processes in a configuration management plan. CM-03 sets which changes are controlled, approves them with a security impact analysis and keeps records, and CM-03(02) tests, validates and documents changes. CM-04 analyses each change for its security and privacy impact before it is made, which supports sorting changes by risk. AC-05 documents the duties to keep apart, such as development, testing and release, and SA-10 has the developer make only approved changes and document their security impact.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the policy to cover how customers learn of changes and of their duty to cooperate. Add rules for emergency changes at the normal security level and for correcting unexpected effects of a change.

clauses.title: Role-based training on secure delivery and malicious code
clauses.rationale: AT-03 gives role-based security training to set roles before they take up duties and at a set frequency, and keeps its content up to date, which covers secure development and delivery and the tools used. AT-02 gives security literacy training and awareness to all users, contractors included, and updates its content, which covers the risks of malicious code.

clauses.title: Documented design of security functions, based on analysis
clauses.rationale: SA-17 requires the developer to produce a design specification and security architecture that describe the required security functions accurately and completely. SA-11(02) has the developer carry out threat modelling and vulnerability analyses, which is the security analysis behind the design.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the design documents to state what each security feature takes in and returns, and which errors it can raise. It also asks for an analysis of how well each feature is likely to work. Add both to the SA-17 design specification.

clauses.title: Assessing the risk of each change before release
clauses.rationale: CM-04 analyses each change for its possible security and privacy impact before it is made, which is the risk assessment of the change. CM-03 reviews proposed changes and approves or rejects them with that analysis in view, which lets the provider require mitigation of a high-risk change before it reaches production.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the combined effects of changes made at the same time to be assessed, and for the risks found to be ranked. Add both to the CM-04 analysis. Send customers details of the highest-risk changes in advance, so they can assess the risk themselves.

clauses.title: Risk-based, documented tests before changes go live
clauses.rationale: CM-03(02) tests, validates and documents changes before they are finalised. SA-11 has the developer test at a set depth and coverage, produce evidence of the results and fix the flaws found, and SA-11(07) verifies the scope of that testing. SA-03(02) approves, documents and controls the use of live data in preproduction environments, and SI-19 removes set personal data elements from datasets, which anonymises customer data used in tests. CA-08 runs penetration tests on set systems, which covers the optional tests before launch.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the customer's approval before its data is used in tests, and for customers to take part in tests where the contract says so. Record for each test of a security feature its description, starting conditions, expected outcome and the steps to run it.

clauses.title: Tracing every production change to who made it
clauses.rationale: CM-05 defines, approves and enforces access restrictions for changes, and CM-05(01) enforces them automatically and keeps audit records, which applies a rights framework to version control and deployment tools. AU-12 generates audit records for the defined events, and AU-03 requires each record to show the identity of the people or components involved, which traces each change to its source. CM-03 keeps records of controlled changes and monitors change activity, which supports the optional monitoring of production changes.

clauses.title: Tracking every software and configuration change, with rollback
clauses.rationale: SA-10 has the developer document, manage and control the integrity of changes to configuration items, and SA-10(05) keeps the integrity of the mapping used for version control. CM-09 defines the configuration items and places them under configuration management, which brings software and configurations into scope. CM-02 keeps a current baseline configuration, and CM-02(03) retains earlier configurations to support rollback.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for safeguards that keep customer data intact and available when a component is rolled back to an earlier state. Add them to the rollback procedure.

clauses.title: Approving changes before they reach production
clauses.rationale: CM-03 reviews proposed changes and approves or rejects them, documents the decisions and monitors change activity, which covers approval before release and the optional monitoring of the approval process. SA-10 requires the developer to implement only changes the organisation has approved.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for customers to take part in releases as their contracts set out. Add that step to the CM-03 release procedure.

clauses.title: Risk-based protection of non-production environments
clauses.rationale: RA-03 assesses threats and vulnerabilities and the likely harm, which covers the risk assessment of development and test environments. SA-03(01) protects preproduction environments in line with risk across the life cycle. CP-09 backs up user-level and system-level information at a set frequency, which extends the backups to the parts of these environments that need them.

clauses.title: Keeping production apart from test and development
clauses.rationale: SC-32 places system components in separate physical or logical domains, which keeps production apart from test and development. CM-04(01) analyses changes in a separate test environment before they reach operations. SA-03(02) approves, documents and controls any use of live data in preproduction environments, which governs customer data in test or development.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the customer's explicit approval before production data is used in test or development. It also asks the provider to keep production keys and secrets out of other environments, and to document and justify any reuse it has to make.

clauses.title: Keeping a software bill of materials up to date
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an inventory of system components at the level of detail needed for tracking and reporting, and updates it at a set frequency, which can hold the list of software components. SR-04 documents, monitors and maintains the provenance of set components and their data, which records where each software component came from.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a component list for every software component the provider develops or integrates. Treat an integrated component as an exception only when its list cannot reasonably be produced, and handle its risk through the exception process.

clauses.title: Rules for outside and open-source software and hardware
clauses.rationale: CM-01 and SR-01 have the provider document and share policies and procedures for configuration management and supply chain risk, which hold the rules for third-party and open-source software. CM-10 uses software in line with contracts and licences, and CM-10(01) restricts the use of open-source software. SR-04 documents and maintains the provenance of set components, which supports the list of dependencies. CM-14 blocks installation of set software unless its digital signature is verified against an approved certificate, and SR-11 detects and keeps out counterfeit components, which together check that software is genuine. SR-05(02) assesses components before they are selected or accepted, which covers the optional risk assessment of each product.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for third-party software to come from trusted sources. Name the approved sources in the policy and use them for every download.

clauses.title: Handling emergency changes and other exceptions safely
clauses.rationale: CM-03 sets which types of change fall under change control, and reviews and approves each one with a security impact analysis. Its documented decisions and change records give a starting point for handling emergency changes and other exceptions.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a set procedure for exceptions, emergency changes included, that keeps their risks in check. Add it to the CM-03 change process.

clauses.title: Rules for overseeing suppliers that help run the service
clauses.rationale: SA-01 and SR-01 have the provider document and share policies and procedures for acquisition and supply chain risk, which hold the rules for service organisations. SR-06 assesses and reviews the supply chain risks of suppliers and contractors, and SA-09 requires external service providers to meet the provider's security requirements, defines oversight roles and monitors their compliance. SA-04 writes the security requirements and the split of responsibility into the acquisition contract, and SR-03(03) passes those controls down to subcontractors. SR-08 sets agreements with supply chain partners on notice of compromises and on the results of assessments or audits, which covers the optional independent audit reports.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to classify service organisations by risk and to decide which count as subservice organisations. Add both steps to the SR-06 assessment.

clauses.title: Assessing supplier risk before and during use
clauses.rationale: SR-06 assesses and reviews, at a set frequency, the supply chain risks of suppliers and contractors and of what they provide, which covers the assessment of each service organisation and its regular review. RA-03 judges the likelihood and size of harm to the information a system handles, and RA-03(01) applies the assessment to supply chain risks, which covers protection needs and the impact of a breach.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the assessment to weigh dependence on the supplier and the risk of lock-in. It also asks about the complementary controls expected at subservice organisations, and the data that suppliers' own subcontractors handle. Add these topics to the SR-06 assessment.

clauses.title: Limiting supplier access to customer data
clauses.rationale: AC-06 allows only the access each task needs, and AC-06(06) bars privileged access by users from outside the organisation, which keeps suppliers away from customer data. RA-03 judges the likelihood and size of harm from unauthorised access to or disclosure of information, which is the risk assessment needed before an exception. MA-05 has authorised, competent staff supervise the maintenance work of people who lack the required authorisations, which covers supervised supplier work.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the customer's written authorisation before a service organisation processes its data, given per supplier or in advance for all. Add this to the customer contract.

clauses.title: A reviewed register of suppliers and their details
clauses.rationale: SA-09 defines and documents the provider's oversight roles and responsibilities for each external service, which covers the responsible contacts. SA-09(05) addresses where external providers process and store data and run their services, which relates to the data locations in the register.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a register of service organisations with details such as head office, jurisdiction, data locations, risk class, start of use and proof of compliance. Keep that register and review it at least once a year for completeness and accuracy.

clauses.title: Ongoing checks that suppliers meet their security duties
clauses.rationale: SA-09 monitors the control compliance of external service providers on an ongoing basis, using methods the provider sets. SR-06 reviews supplier risks at a set frequency, which lets the monitoring follow each supplier's risk class, and SR-06(01) adds testing and analysis. SR-08 sets agreements with supply chain partners to receive notice of compromises and the results of assessments or audits, which brings in the reports to review. RA-07 responds to findings from assessments, monitoring and audits in line with risk tolerance, which covers the treatment of deviations.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for assurance that each subservice organisation runs the complementary controls the provider relies on. Add those checks to the SA-09 monitoring. When a change at a supplier significantly weakens the provider's security, tell all customers promptly.

clauses.title: Exit plans for suppliers the provider depends on heavily
clauses.rationale: CP-02 develops a contingency plan that keeps essential functions going through a disruption, compromise or failure and assigns roles and responsibilities. CP-02(07) coordinates that plan with the plans of external service providers, which ties exit planning to the continuity plans.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a documented exit strategy for each service the provider depends on very heavily. Cover the cost and timing of a move to another supplier, the roles and resources for it, success criteria and the indicators that would trigger withdrawal.

clauses.title: Telling customers which suppliers handle their data
clauses.rationale: CA-03 approves and manages information exchanges with other systems through agreements. Each agreement documents the interface characteristics, security requirements, controls and responsibilities, and CA-03 reviews the agreements at a set frequency, which covers the data flows and interfaces with service organisations.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to tell customers which service organisations and subcontractors it uses and which types of data each one processes. Publish this list to customers and keep it current.

clauses.title: Approving each transfer between components and their vendors
clauses.rationale: AC-01 and SR-01 have the provider document and share policies and procedures for access control and supply chain risk, which hold the rule on exchanges with suppliers. AC-04 enforces approved authorisations for information flows between the system and connected systems, so only approved flows pass between a component and its supplier. SC-07 connects to outside systems only through managed interfaces, which blocks direct links between components and their suppliers. AU-02 names the proposed operations, checks and transfers as events to log, and AU-12 generates the records that form the trace.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for approval of the content itself before every transfer to or from a component's supplier. Add a per-transfer approval step to the AC-04 flow rules.

clauses.title: How the provider prepares for and handles security incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-01 has the provider document and share an incident response policy and procedures. IR-08 builds a response plan that sets the structure of the response capability, defines reportable incidents and assigns responsibility, which covers the response team and gives a starting point for classifying incidents. IR-04 handles incidents from preparation through detection and analysis to containment, eradication and recovery, and coordinates with contingency planning, and IR-04(12) adds forensic analysis for collecting evidence. IR-06 has staff report suspected incidents to the response capability within a set time, and sends incident information to authorities the provider defines.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for set channels to reach customers and for timely notice to those affected by an incident. Name the channels in the IR-08 plan, and add guidelines for classifying, prioritising and escalating incidents and for finding their root causes.

clauses.title: Approved plans for each stage of incident response
clauses.rationale: IR-08 builds an incident response plan, has set roles review and approve it and sends it to response staff. IR-08 also updates the plan for system and organisational changes and communicates each change. IR-04 covers preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery, and feeds lessons learned back into procedures, training and testing, which are the stages the plans must address.

clauses.title: Analysing incidents to their root cause and keeping evidence
clauses.rationale: IR-04 covers detection and analysis and feeds lessons learned back, IR-04(04) correlates incident information, and IR-04(11) and IR-04(12) provide an integrated response team and forensic analysis. IR-08 defines reportable incidents, which gives the catalogue used to classify them, and IR-05 tracks and documents each incident. AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised access, change and deletion, and AU-11 keeps audit records long enough for later investigation and for regulatory retention. IR-07(02) sets up coordination with external providers, which covers calling in outside help, and IR-03 tests the response capability at a set frequency, which covers the optional yearly exercises.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to choose outside incident responders for their competence and trustworthiness, or on a national cyber security authority's advice. Add those criteria to the IR-07 arrangements. Monitor the incident handling process itself and correct deviations promptly.

clauses.title: Sharing incident outcomes with affected customers
clauses.rationale: IR-05 tracks and documents incidents, which records how each one was resolved. IR-08 has the response plan address the sharing of incident information, and IR-08(01) covers breaches. IR-06 sends incident information to authorities the provider defines.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to send each affected customer the documented solution for acknowledgement or confirmation. It also asks the contract to set which data customers receive for their own analysis of an incident. Add both to the IR-08 plan and the customer contract.

clauses.title: Making staff and partners report events to one central point
clauses.rationale: IR-06 requires staff to report suspected incidents to the incident response capability within a set time. SR-08 sets agreements with supply chain partners to notify compromises, which places a reporting duty on business partners. AT-02 trains users, and AT-02(02) and AT-02(03) cover insider threat and social engineering, which helps staff recognise what to report. IR-07 provides a support resource that advises users on handling and reporting incidents, which makes the reporting route known.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to assure staff that false alarms are safe to report. Explain the reporting channels to customers and service organisations as well as to staff.

clauses.title: Learning from incidents through a knowledge base
clauses.rationale: IR-05 tracks and documents incidents, and IR-05(01) automates their tracking, data collection and analysis, which builds the knowledge repository and measures incident types. IR-04 feeds lessons learned from incident handling into procedures, training and testing and puts the resulting changes in place. IR-06 reports incident information to set authorities, which covers reports to supporting bodies.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to use the knowledge repository to spot recurring incidents and to extend the incident classification catalogue. Add both uses to the IR-04 lessons learned process.

clauses.title: Running continuity management under a senior owner
clauses.rationale: CP-01 has the provider document and share a contingency planning policy and procedures that address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities and management commitment, and names an official to manage them. CP-02 develops a contingency plan that identifies essential functions, sets recovery objectives, assigns roles and coordinates with incident handling, which covers the plans and their link to incident management.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a continuity management system run to ISO 22301 or BSI 200-4. Name a member of top management as its process owner, with enough resources, and have leaders show visible support for it.

clauses.title: Assessing the impact of disruption on critical services
clauses.rationale: CP-02 identifies essential functions and their contingency requirements and sets recovery objectives, restoration priorities and metrics, and CP-02(08) identifies critical assets. RA-03 identifies threats and vulnerabilities and judges the likelihood and size of harm, which supplies risk-based scenarios. RA-09 identifies critical system components and functions through a criticality analysis.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for a business impact analysis that sets the maximum tolerable downtime and estimates the resources needed to resume. It also maps dependencies on partners and third parties. Review the analysis at least once a year and after major changes.

clauses.title: Documented plans to keep the service running
clauses.rationale: CP-02 develops a contingency plan with roles, responsibilities and contacts that keeps essential functions going and restores the system in full. It coordinates the plan with incident handling, has it approved and sends it to key staff, then reviews it at a set frequency and updates it for changes.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the plans to cover notice to customers and to stay consistent across all locations, zones and regions. Add both to the CP-02 plan.

clauses.title: Yearly continuity tests that include customers
clauses.rationale: CP-04 tests the contingency plan at a set frequency, reviews the results and starts corrective action, and CP-04(01) coordinates the tests with the owners of related plans. CP-02 updates the plan for problems found in testing and feeds lessons learned into future testing and training.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for affected customers and relevant third parties to take part in the tests. Tell customers in advance about tests that could affect them, with the timing and an assessment of the likely impact, and review the alarm and notification plan after each exercise.

clauses.title: Listing the requirements that apply and how they are met
clauses.rationale: PM-01 develops a security programme plan that gives an overview of the programme's requirements and of the controls in place or planned to meet them. PL-02 builds a security plan for the system with an overview of its security requirements and a description of the controls that meet them, which records how the provider complies.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to name each legal, regulatory, self-imposed and contractual requirement and the procedure that meets it. Record these in the PL-02 plan, and give customers an overview of the procedures when they ask.

clauses.title: A multi-year audit programme that protects the live service
clauses.rationale: CA-01 has the provider document and share an assessment, authorisation and monitoring policy with procedures, which holds the audit rules. CA-02 selects assessors and develops an assessment plan with scope and procedures. PM-14 keeps plans for security testing and monitoring developed, carried out and reviewed against the risk strategy, which supports a programme over several years. CA-08 runs penetration tests at a set frequency, which covers intrusion tests of external access points, and SA-11(04) and SA-11(01) cover manual code review and static analysis of security features.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the audit rules to protect the running service: auditors get read-only access, and disruptive work runs in maintenance windows or outside peak hours. It also asks for audit activities to be logged and monitored. Add these rules to the CA-01 procedures, and grant customers information and audit rights in their contracts.

clauses.title: Yearly impartial internal audits with risk-based follow-up
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses controls at a set frequency to find whether they meet the security requirements, and CA-02(01) uses independent assessors, which supports impartial internal audits. RA-07 responds to findings from assessments and audits in line with risk tolerance, and CA-05 records and tracks the remediation of weaknesses found. CA-07 sets up continuous monitoring with ongoing assessments and metrics, and CA-07(06) adds automation, which covers the optional automatic monitoring and reporting of deviations.
clauses.gaps: C5's optional criteria ask for interfaces that let customers check selected contract terms in real time. Offer them to customers if you adopt those criteria.

clauses.title: Reporting security performance to top management
clauses.rationale: PM-06 develops, monitors and reports on measures of security performance, which provides the metrics. PM-31 runs organisation-wide continuous monitoring with set metrics and reports the security status of systems to set roles at a set frequency, which keeps top management informed.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks top management to review the ISMS at least once a year, using this performance information. Add that review, and yearly reports from business units on how well their policies and procedures work.

clauses.title: Legal review of government requests for data
clauses.rationale: PT-02 determines and documents the authority that permits each kind of processing of personal data, and restricts processing to what that authority allows. For a request from a government agency, this calls for a recorded check of the legal basis before personal customer data is disclosed.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks experts to make and document a legal assessment of every government request before any customer, derived or account data is accessed or disclosed, personal or otherwise. Add this step to the procedure for handling such requests.

clauses.title: Telling customers about government requests for their data
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 sets controls for protecting an organisation's own systems, and a duty to tell customers about government requests lies outside that scope. C5 asks the provider to inform affected customers promptly when an authority asks for their data, with exceptions where the law behind the request forbids it or there are clear signs of illegal use of the service. Add this notice to the procedure for government requests.

clauses.title: Giving agencies only the data a request covers
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access, and AC-03(09) validates information before it is released, which keeps investigators to the data in scope. SI-19 removes set personal data elements from datasets, and SI-19(04) masks or replaces direct identifiers, which supports anonymising or pseudonymising data mixed with that of other customers. AU-06 reviews audit records for inappropriate or unusual activity, which covers the optional monitoring of what investigators do.
clauses.gaps: Where the requested data is mixed with other customers' data, C5 asks for anonymisation or pseudonymisation so agencies can link it only to the customers named in the request. Apply this to every type of customer data, and correct promptly any deviation found while monitoring investigators.

clauses.title: Documenting for customers how data is disclosed to authorities
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 sets controls for protecting an organisation's own systems, and explaining disclosure practice to customers lies outside that scope. C5 asks for a document per service that sets out the disclosure process, the technical limits, the logging and how customers can review the logs, and the laws that govern notice to customers. Publish this document to customers and keep it current.

clauses.title: Guidance that helps customers configure and use the service securely
clauses.rationale: SA-05 provides administrator documentation on secure configuration and operation and on the effective use of security functions. It also provides user documentation on the security functions, secure ways of using the system and the user's own security duties, and distributes both to set roles, which covers the guidance and the controls customers must run themselves.
clauses.gaps: C5's optional criterion asks the provider to warn customers in good time about planned changes to the service, so they can prepare. Add that notice to the change process.

clauses.title: Finding vulnerabilities during development by testing and review
clauses.rationale: SA-11 has the developer test the system and run a verifiable flaw remediation process, with SA-11(01) for static code analysis, SA-11(08) for dynamic code analysis and SA-11(04) for manual code reviews. RA-05 scans the system and hosted applications for vulnerabilities, including when new ones are reported, and fixes them in line with an assessment of risk, which covers flaws in third-party libraries. CA-08(01) uses an independent agent or team for penetration testing, which covers the optional yearly tests by outside experts.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for security checks driven by the software bill of materials. Add these checks to the RA-05 scanning.

clauses.title: Publishing known vulnerabilities and fixes to customers
clauses.rationale: SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside organisations, generates its own and shares them with set external organisations, which covers reading supplier advisories and informing customers. RA-05 uses standards to enumerate software flaws and measure their impact, and shares what vulnerability monitoring finds with set roles, which supports CVE references and CVSS scores. SI-02 identifies, reports and corrects flaws and installs security updates within a set time, and SI-02(05) adds automatic updates, which fits the optional update mechanism.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for advisories that sort vulnerabilities into known-exploited, patched and unfixed ones, with the reason a fix is withheld, and score them with CVSS and with EPSS, SSVC or a similar system. Check supplier vulnerability information at least daily, and use the CSAF format for advisories if you adopt the optional criterion.

clauses.title: Logs and error reports that customers can use and control
clauses.rationale: AU-02 selects the event types to log and records why they are enough for later investigation, which ties logging to the identified risks. AU-03 makes each record show the type of event, when and where it happened, its source and outcome and who was involved. AU-12 generates the records and lets set roles choose which event types each component logs, and AU-09 protects audit information from unauthorised access, change and deletion. AU-16 coordinates audit information with external organisations when it crosses organisational boundaries, which supports delivering logs to a customer's SIEM. SI-11 produces error messages that support corrective action while keeping exploitable detail hidden.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for customers to be able to delete their own logs, and for logging of customer actions on the management plane to cover every relevant component. Build both into the logging design.

clauses.title: Multi-factor sign-in that customers can enforce
clauses.rationale: IA-08 uniquely identifies and authenticates users and processes from outside the organisation, which covers the customers' users, components and applications at every access point. IA-02(01) and IA-02(02) add multi-factor authentication and IA-02(13) adds out-of-band authentication. IA-02 is written for the organisation's own users, so these enhancements apply to customer users by analogy.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for the service to let customers enforce multi-factor authentication for their own privileged users, components and applications. Offer that setting to customers.

clauses.title: Secure sessions that end after inactivity
clauses.rationale: SC-23 protects the authenticity of communication sessions, and SC-23(01) and SC-23(03) invalidate session identifiers at logout and use unique identifiers generated by the system, which guards against hijacking and replay. AC-12 automatically ends a user session after set conditions, such as a period of inactivity.

clauses.title: Password rules and tools the provider offers customers
clauses.rationale: IA-05 verifies the recipient's identity when an authenticator is first issued and protects authenticator content, and IA-05(01) sets the rules for password-based authentication. AC-09(03) notifies users of changes to their account, such as a password reset. SA-05 gives users documentation on their security duties, which shares the password rules with customers. IA-08 authenticates users from outside the organisation, the customer users these rules protect.
clauses.gaps: C5 limits an initial password to 14 days and a reset procedure to 48 hours. Set both limits in IA-05, and give customers tools to manage and enforce the password rules for their users.

clauses.title: Self-service roles and access rights for customer users
clauses.rationale: AC-02 defines account types, group and role membership and the privileges of each account, and reviews accounts, which the service can offer so customers manage, list and review their users' rights. AC-03(07) enforces access through roles. AC-05 defines access authorisations that support separation of duties, and AC-06 allows only the access each task needs. These controls describe the provider's own accounts, so they apply to the customer functions by analogy.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for these functions as self-service features for customers. Offer customers tools to manage roles and to list and review their users' rights.

clauses.title: Checking every action against the user's permissions
clauses.rationale: AC-03 enforces approved authorisations for logical access, and AC-03(13) adds attribute-based access control. AC-24 applies access control decisions to each access request before access is enforced. SA-11 tests new and changed functions at a set depth and coverage and corrects the flaws found, which validates the authorisation mechanisms before release. CM-04(02) checks after a change that the affected controls still work as intended.

clauses.title: Keeping customer data confidential in virtual networks
clauses.rationale: AC-04 enforces approved information flows within the system, and AC-04(21) separates flows by physical or logical means, which keeps customer traffic apart in software-defined networks. SC-07 monitors and controls traffic at managed interfaces, and SC-07(20) adds dynamic isolation and segregation. SA-11 tests new and changed features before release and corrects the flaws found, which covers validating SDN features.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for defects found in SDN features to be assessed and fixed in order of risk. Rank the SA-11 findings by risk before correcting them.

clauses.title: Hardened, traceable machine and container images
clauses.rationale: CM-06 sets and applies the most restrictive configuration settings based on common secure configurations, which hardens the images the provider supplies. CM-07(05) lets only authorised software run, which supports limiting customer users to released images. SR-04 documents and maintains the provenance of components, which supports labelling images with their origin. CM-14 blocks installation of set components unless their digital signature is verified against an approved certificate. SI-07 detects unauthorised changes to software, with SI-07(09) verifying the boot process, which covers integrity checks at startup and during runtime.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks the provider to tell customers what changed from the previous version of each image it supplies. Report the results of integrity checks to customers as well, as the optional criteria ask.

clauses.title: Keeping customer data in the regions the contract names
clauses.rationale: CM-12 identifies and documents where set information is processed and stored and on which components, and records any change of location, which tracks the regions that hold customer data. SA-09(05) restricts where external providers process and store data and run their services, which keeps service organisations within the customer's chosen regions.
clauses.gaps: C5 asks for an architecture that keeps customer data and its backups in the contracted regions. Set the regions and the terms for changing them in the contract, and tell customers before any change. For the optional partitions, keep identity management, privileged access, logging and key handling inside the chosen partition.
